content.comment_body: I'm developing an automatic switching program using [product_name] modules [article_no] and [article_no]. The demo program is finished and runs on the controller. However, I'm encountering an issue: Relays Q1-Q4 on one [product_name] module operate normally in both auto and manual modes, but relays Q5 and Q6 only work when the LAN port of the controller is connected to a PC or network switch. It's unusual because I expect the outputs to function without a network connection. My program doesn't use any network I/O and relies solely on hard-wired digital inputs/outputs plus one analog input. I've attached the program for reference. Can someone help explain this behavior and provide a solution?
Please avoid submitting duplicate posts about the same issue. You also created another topic regarding the [product_name] modules [article_no] and [article_no].

This thread is closed due to repeated postings of the same question. The second topic titled about the [product_name] modules [article_no] and [article_no] was published in the hardware section. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports an unexpected dependency where certain output relays (Q5, Q6) only activate when the controller is connected to a network, despite not using network I/O in the program and relying exclusively on local hard-wired inputs and outputs. Other outputs (Q1-Q4) work correctly regardless of network status, leading to confusion about the hardware's standalone functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects all outputs on the controller to operate according to the programmed logic independently of the network connection, since only local inputs and outputs have been configured.
